boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Purdue spaces with documented ways to study, create, play, or gather alongside other students.

cards.title: Purdue Memorial Union
cards.subtitle: 101 N. Grant St.
cards.notes: Use the union as a central between-class stop: its spaces support eating, lounging, studying and getting fresh air.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus hub with room for everyday pauses and meetups.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue describes the Memorial Union as a student hangout with areas to eat, lounge, do homework and get fresh air.
cards.access_notes: Building access and individual venue availability may vary.

cards.title: Purdue Memorial Union Outdoor Terraces
cards.subtitle: Purdue Memorial Union
cards.notes: Bring a book or meet a project partner outside; the terraces were designed for eating, meeting, studying and socializing.
cards.short_summary: Outdoor union seating with dedicated space for shared campus activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue says the Memorial Union’s outdoor terraces provide space to eat, meet, study and socialize.
cards.source_title: PMU renovations combine modern flair, nods to Purdue history
cards.access_notes: Outdoor conditions and event setups can affect availability.

cards.title: Boiler Game Mine
cards.subtitle: Purdue Memorial Union basement
cards.notes: Plan a casual console or PC session with classmates, or check whether an esports event is using the shared gaming space.
cards.short_summary: Purdue’s campus gaming facility supports both casual and competitive play.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue identifies Boiler Game Mine as an on-campus esports and gaming facility with PC and console gaming, competition and casual play.
cards.access_notes: Gaming availability varies; the official page lists walk-in and reservation rates.

cards.title: Union Rack and Roll
cards.subtitle: Purdue Memorial Union basement
cards.notes: Organize a low-key group outing around bowling, HyperBowling or billiards, and confirm open-play availability before heading down.
cards.short_summary: A basement recreation venue for group bowling and billiards.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue says Union Rack and Roll offers bowling, HyperBowling, billiards, group and open-play opportunities.
cards.access_notes: Open play and reservations are subject to availability; official rates are posted.

cards.title: Hicks Undergraduate Library
cards.subtitle: Purdue Libraries
cards.notes: Choose Hicks when you need an interactive learning and study setting; check the library’s current hours before making the walk.
cards.short_summary: An undergraduate library with study space, classrooms and a computer lab.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue describes Hicks as a place for interactive learning and studying, with classrooms, study-break events and a computer lab.
cards.source_title: The Top 10 Best Study Locations at Purdue
cards.access_notes: Consult current Purdue Libraries hours and room-access information before visiting.

cards.title: Wilmeth Active Learning Center
cards.subtitle: WALC
cards.notes: Set up for classwork in this central academic building, then reserve a study room in advance when your group needs a room.
cards.short_summary: A campus hub for classrooms and study space with reservable rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue says WALC serves as a central hub for classrooms and study spaces; its study rooms are available by reservation.
cards.access_notes: Study rooms require reservation; walk-in availability is not guaranteed.

cards.title: Krach Leadership Center
cards.subtitle: Krach Center for Leadership
cards.notes: Bring collaborators for a group-work session in the open-plan center, which includes conference, event and student-organization space.
cards.short_summary: A collaboration-oriented building built around team and organization work.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue describes Krach as an open-plan hub for collaborative work with conference rooms, special-event areas and student-organization space.
cards.source_title: The Top 10 Best Study Locations at Purdue
cards.access_notes: Some rooms and organization spaces may have restricted or reserved access.

cards.title: Black Cultural Center Library
cards.subtitle: Black Cultural Center, Room 219
cards.notes: Pair focused reading with time to explore the collection and exhibited art; plan around the center’s currently posted access schedule.
cards.short_summary: A culture-centered library with study and collaboration resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue says the Black Cultural Center Library has a special collection, computer lab, student collaboration spots and art on exhibit.
cards.source_title: The Top 10 Best Study Locations at Purdue
cards.access_notes: Verify current Black Cultural Center library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Leighty Commons
cards.subtitle: Wetherill Laboratory of Chemistry
cards.notes: Pause by the Nobel display and LED sculpture outside Wetherill Room 200, then use the nearby commons as a campus meeting point.
cards.short_summary: A chemistry-building commons anchored by a prominent science display.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue says Leighty Commons is outside Wetherill Room 200 and that its Nobel display and LED sculpture are a campus photo destination.
cards.access_notes: Commons access may follow Wetherill Laboratory building access.

cards.title: JamSpace
cards.subtitle: Lower level, Elliott Hall of Music
cards.notes: Registered students can book a band rehearsal and use the room’s amps, keyboard, drum kit, mixing board and small PA system.
cards.short_summary: A student-band rehearsal room equipped for ensemble practice and recording.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue says JamSpace in Elliott Hall is available to registered students and is outfitted with instruments, amps, recording connectivity and PA equipment.
cards.source_title: New music rehearsal space opens for students
cards.access_notes: Available to registered Purdue students; booking is required through the linked Purdue process.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission activities listed by Purdue’s public events calendar for campus and the immediate Lafayette–West Lafayette community.

cards.entity_name: Purdue Varsity Glee Club presents First Nighter
cards.title: Hear First Nighter
cards.subtitle: Loeb Playhouse, Stewart Center — September 4, 2026
cards.notes: Reserve a free ticket for the 7–9 p.m. performance, then arrive at Loeb Playhouse in Stewart Center before the program begins.
cards.short_summary: A free opening-night performance by Purdue’s Varsity Glee Club.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue lists First Nighter as a free event with ticket reservation required.
cards.source_title: Purdue Varsity Glee Club presents First Nighter
cards.access_notes: September 4, 2026, 7–9 p.m.; free ticket reservation required.

cards.title: Catch a Mucca Pazza pop-up
cards.subtitle: Purdue West Lafayette campus — September 10, 2026
cards.notes: Check the event listing before heading out, then join one of the roaming pop-up performances during Weeks of Welcome.
cards.short_summary: Free campus pop-up performances by the Chicago ensemble Mucca Pazza.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue says Mucca Pazza will provide free pop-up performances around the West Lafayette campus.
cards.access_notes: September 10, 2026; campus locations are pop-up and should be checked near the event date.

cards.title: Attend Purduette Premiere
cards.subtitle: Loeb Playhouse, Stewart Center — September 11, 2026
cards.notes: Make a free reservation, then meet up at Loeb Playhouse for the Purduettes’ season-opening performance at 7:30 p.m.
cards.short_summary: A free, reservation-required evening concert introducing the year’s Purduettes.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue lists Purduette Premiere as free with a reservation required.
cards.access_notes: September 11, 2026, 7:30–9 p.m.; free reservation required.

cards.title: Browse the Latino Festival
cards.subtitle: Lafayette — September 12, 2026
cards.notes: Go between noon and 5 p.m. to take in the live entertainment and community organizations; buying from vendors is optional.
cards.short_summary: A free annual community festival with entertainment, organizations, and cultural activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue’s listing says the Tippecanoe Latino Festival is free and open to all.
cards.access_notes: September 12, 2026, noon–5 p.m.; vendors are present, but admission is free.

cards.title: Spend an afternoon at Global Fest
cards.subtitle: Downtown West Lafayette — September 19, 2026
cards.notes: Head downtown for the afternoon performances and cultural activities; the Purdue calendar identifies the event as free.
cards.short_summary: A free downtown gathering of performances, cultural exhibits, and activities during Weeks of Welcome.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue lists the 31st Annual West Lafayette Global Fest as a free event.
cards.access_notes: September 19, 2026, beginning at 3 p.m. in downtown West Lafayette.

cards.title: Try the archaeology activities
cards.subtitle: Tippecanoe Battlefield Park and Museum — September 19, 2026
cards.notes: Plan a daytime trip for the hands-on archaeology activities, artifact identification, and museum entry included with the free event.
cards.short_summary: A free all-ages archaeology event with hands-on activities and museum entry.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue lists this event at $0 and says it includes free entry to the Tippecanoe Battlefield Museum.
cards.access_notes: September 19, 2026, 10 a.m.–2 p.m.; held at 200 Battle Ground Avenue in Battle Ground.

cards.title: Listen at Star City Nights
cards.subtitle: Downtown Lafayette — September 25–26, 2026
cards.notes: Meet at the downtown main stage for the free live and indie performances; browsing the vendor market does not require a purchase.
cards.short_summary: A free downtown evening of live music, performances, and a vendor market.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue states that Star City Nights is free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: September 25, 2026, 6 p.m.–midnight; downtown Lafayette at 600 Main Street.

cards.title: Walk Art on the Wabash
cards.subtitle: Tapawingo Park — September 27, 2026
cards.notes: Walk the Wabash-side art fair from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. and view artists’ work; food purchases are optional.
cards.short_summary: A free Tapawingo Park art fair featuring artists from fifteen counties.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue lists Art on the Wabash 2026 as a free event at Tapawingo Park.
cards.access_notes: September 27, 2026, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; Tapawingo Park, 100 Tapawingo Drive.

cards.title: Watch the Spring Showcase
cards.subtitle: Ross-Ade Stadium — April 11, 2026
cards.notes: For the next listed spring showcase, confirm the current schedule before going; Purdue’s 2026 listing identified public entry as free.
cards.short_summary: A free public opportunity to watch Purdue football’s spring showcase at Ross-Ade Stadium.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue’s 2026 Spring Showcase listing states the event was free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: The cited 2026 event occurred April 11 at noon; verify a future showcase date before travel.

cards.entity_name: Purdue Bands & Orchestras Presents Jazz on the Hill
cards.title: See Jazz on the Hill
cards.subtitle: Slayter Center of Performing Arts — May 3, 2026
cards.notes: Use the Bands & Orchestras schedule to confirm a future date, then bring a group to the Slayter outdoor performance space.
cards.short_summary: A free Purdue Bands & Orchestras outdoor jazz performance at Slayter.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue’s event listing says all Purdue Bands & Orchestras concerts are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Purdue Bands & Orchestras Presents Jazz on the Hill
cards.access_notes: The cited 2026 event occurred May 3; confirm a future concert date before travel.

warnings: Two annual-style campus events cited here occurred earlier in 2026; their access notes direct visitors to verify a future date before travel.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct Purdue environments for individual work, group work, course support, and project-based study.

cards.entity_name: Grand Reading Room, Wilmeth Active Learning Center
cards.title: Grand Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Wilmeth Active Learning Center
cards.notes: Set up in the reading room when you want a library setting with views toward the clock tower; use the building’s posted access information before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A named reading room inside Purdue’s central active-learning library.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue identifies the Grand Reading Room, with views of the clock tower, among WALC’s study and collaborative spaces.
cards.source_title: Thomas S. and Harvey D. Wilmeth Active Learning Center
cards.access_notes: Purdue describes WALC as a student-centered facility with study spaces; verify current building access before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Study Rooms, Wilmeth Active Learning Center
cards.title: WALC Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Wilmeth Active Learning Center
cards.notes: Reserve a WALC study room for a focused small-group session, and do not count on a walk-in room being available when you arrive.
cards.short_summary: Reservable rooms in the active-learning center.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue Libraries states that WALC study rooms are available by reservation and that walk-in availability is not guaranteed.
cards.access_notes: Study rooms are described as reservable; verify the current room-reservation process and library hours before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Humanities, Social Sciences and Education Library
cards.title: HSSE Library
cards.subtitle: Stewart Center
cards.notes: Choose the floor that fits your work: Purdue added flexible seating across the first three floors for solo work, groups, and larger groups.
cards.short_summary: A renovated Stewart Center library with varied seating formats.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue Libraries reports adding more than 200 seats across HSSE’s first, second, and third floors, with options for individual, group, and large-group work.
cards.source_title: Purdue Libraries and School of Information Studies Annual Report 2024
cards.access_notes: Purdue’s study-space page describes second- and third-floor small group rooms as first come, first served, while the first-floor room is reservable; confirm current conditions.

cards.title: Mathematical Sciences Library
cards.subtitle: Mathematical Sciences Building
cards.notes: Bring a problem set and work with classmates in a group study room; Purdue lists these rooms as first come, first served.
cards.short_summary: A mathematics-building library with group study rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue Libraries lists group study rooms in the Mathematical Sciences Library as open on a first-come, first-served basis.
cards.access_notes: Purdue’s page describes group rooms as first come, first served; check current library hours before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Roland G. Parrish Library of Management and Economics
cards.title: Parrish Library Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Krannert Building
cards.notes: Book a room in Parrish Library when your work benefits from a dedicated group setting, and confirm the reservation process before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: Reservable study rooms in Purdue’s management and economics library.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue Libraries states that study rooms at the Roland G. Parrish Library of Management and Economics are available by reservation.
cards.access_notes: Walk-in availability is not guaranteed according to Purdue’s page; verify current reservation details and hours.

cards.title: Veterinary Medical Library
cards.subtitle: Lynn Hall of Veterinary Medicine
cards.notes: Use the refreshed library when you need flexible seating or a group room; reserve ahead instead of relying on an open walk-in room.
cards.short_summary: A Lynn Hall library updated with more open and group-study seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue Libraries reports that the Veterinary Medical Library’s 2024 refresh increased seating in open-study and group-study rooms by 15%.
cards.source_title: Purdue Libraries and School of Information Studies Annual Report 2024
cards.access_notes: Purdue lists the library’s study rooms as reservable and warns that walk-in availability is not guaranteed; verify current hours and reservations.

cards.title: Aviation and Transportation Technology Library
cards.subtitle: Purdue University Airport Terminal
cards.notes: Use a small group room or conference room for a planned session at the airport-terminal library; rooms are listed as first come, first served.
cards.short_summary: A Purdue library at the airport terminal with small-group options.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue Libraries lists two small group study rooms and one conference room at the Aviation and Transportation Technology Library, first come, first served.
cards.access_notes: Purdue describes the rooms as first come, first served; check current library hours and airport-terminal access before visiting.

cards.entity_name: University Residences Support Center, Shreve Hall
cards.title: Shreve Hall URSC
cards.subtitle: Shreve Hall, 1275 Third Street
cards.notes: If you live in or can appropriately access Shreve Hall, use the URSC’s private study rooms, conference spaces, and computer lab for structured work.
cards.short_summary: A residence-hall support center with private study rooms and computing.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue University Residences lists the University Residences Support Center at Shreve Hall as a student study space with private study rooms, conference spaces, and a computer lab.
cards.access_notes: Located within Shreve Hall; access may be limited to residents or authorized visitors. Contact the hall front desk for current access details.

cards.title: University Hall Commons
cards.subtitle: University Hall
cards.notes: Use the upgraded commons for a study-and-collaboration session, then shift to the nearby student-service areas if you need academic support.
cards.short_summary: A restored campus building with commons and collaboration space.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue reports that University Hall’s completed renovation includes an upgraded commons area and space for students to study and collaborate.
cards.source_title: Restoring Purdue’s University Hall as a student-centered hub
cards.access_notes: Purdue describes the space as student-centered; verify building hours and any event-related restrictions before visiting.

cards.title: Chemistry Resource Room
cards.subtitle: Wetherill Laboratory of Chemistry, Room 117B
cards.notes: Bring chemistry course materials to use the room’s modeling kits, reference books, old exams, and individual or group study space during posted hours.
cards.short_summary: A course-support room with study space and chemistry reference tools.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue lists the Chemistry Resource Room in WTHR 117B as offering modeling kits, reference books, old exams, and individual and group study space.
cards.access_notes: Purdue lists scheduled hours for the room; confirm current hours and eligibility with the Chemistry Resource Room before visiting.

warnings: Several library room-access details come from Purdue’s legacy “Where to Study on Campus” page; each applicable card directs visitors to verify current hours and reservation rules.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along the State Street, Northwestern Avenue, and Tapawingo Drive corridors immediately beside Purdue’s campus.

cards.title: Greyhouse Coffee
cards.subtitle: Northwestern Avenue at State Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the 100 Northwestern Avenue location as a daytime stop; its official page lists this West Lafayette shop and daily hours.
cards.short_summary: A named coffee stop at the Northwestern–State corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Greyhouse Coffee lists a West Lafayette location at 100 Northwestern Ave., Unit A, open daily from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
cards.access_notes: West Lafayette location: 100 Northwestern Ave., Unit A; daily 8 a.m.–5 p.m. Confirm offerings before visiting.

cards.title: Von's Shops
cards.subtitle: West State Street corridor
cards.notes: Browse the used books, records, gifts, and novelty stock at the named shop at 315 West State Street.
cards.short_summary: An independently operated books-and-records stop on State Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Von's Shops identifies its 315 W. State St. location and says it carries used books, vinyl records, gifts, and novelties.
cards.access_notes: 315 W. State St., West Lafayette. Inventory and hours may vary; check the shop before making a special trip.

cards.title: Mad Mushroom
cards.subtitle: West State Street corridor
cards.notes: Plan a meal stop at the Purdue-area location; the restaurant’s location page identifies 320 West State Street.
cards.short_summary: A pizza restaurant directly on the State Street commercial strip.
cards.evidence_claim: Mad Mushroom’s official West Lafayette page lists its address as 320 West State St., West Lafayette, IN 47906.
cards.access_notes: 320 W. State St. The official page publishes operating hours; verify them and menu availability before heading over.

cards.title: Target West Lafayette State Street
cards.subtitle: West State Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the 300 West State Street store for a practical supplies or grocery stop while walking the corridor.
cards.short_summary: A full-service Target location in the State Street retail block.
cards.evidence_claim: Target identifies its West Lafayette State Street store at 300 W. State St., Suite 100, and lists pickup and grocery services.
cards.access_notes: 300 W. State St., Suite 100. Target lists daily store hours on its location page; check the live listing before visiting.

cards.title: University Book Store
cards.subtitle: West State Street corridor
cards.notes: Check the named 360 West State Street store for textbooks, school supplies, Purdue apparel, and postal services.
cards.short_summary: A Purdue-oriented bookstore and supplies stop on State Street.
cards.evidence_claim: University Book Store lists its West Lafayette location at 360 W. State St. and says it carries textbooks, supplies, apparel, and gifts.
cards.access_notes: 360 W. State St. The store lists regular daily hours; confirm semester and holiday hours directly before travel.

cards.title: Wabash Landing 9
cards.subtitle: East State Street / Wabash Landing corridor
cards.notes: Check the current program for a movie or arrange a group screening at the theater at 300 East State Street.
cards.short_summary: A nine-screen cinema in the Wabash Landing section of State Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Visit Lafayette-West Lafayette identifies Wabash Landing 9 at 300 E. State Street and notes its GQT Movies screenings and group events.
cards.access_notes: 300 E. State St. Showtimes, film ratings, and ticket availability change; use the theater’s current ticketing information.

cards.title: Wabash Landing Parking Garage
cards.subtitle: Tapawingo Drive / East State Street corridor
cards.notes: Use this covered city garage when visiting the riverfront corridor; review posted rates and accessible-space details first.
cards.short_summary: A city-owned parking facility serving Wabash Landing and the riverfront.
cards.evidence_claim: West Lafayette says the Wabash Landing Parking Garage at 151 Tapawingo Dr. N. has 680 spaces and offers the first 60 minutes free.
cards.source_title: City of West Lafayette — Wabash Landing Parking Garage
cards.access_notes: 151 Tapawingo Dr. N. The city publishes a 60-minute free period followed by hourly and daily rates; observe posted restrictions.

cards.title: Tapawingo Park
cards.subtitle: Tapawingo Drive riverfront corridor
cards.notes: Walk the paved Wabash Heritage Trail segment and use the scenic overlook, picnic areas, or playground during park hours.
cards.short_summary: A 20-acre riverfront park with trail, playground, and performance amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of West Lafayette describes Tapawingo Park as a roughly 20-acre park with a paved Wabash Heritage Trail segment, playground, scenic overlook, and trails.
cards.source_title: City of West Lafayette — Tapawingo Park
cards.access_notes: 100 Tapawingo Dr. The city lists park hours as 8 a.m. until one-half hour after sunset.

cards.title: Myers Bridge Plaza
cards.subtitle: Tapawingo Drive riverfront corridor
cards.notes: Make this named plaza a waypoint while exploring Tapawingo Park and the riverfront pedestrian connection toward Lafayette.
cards.short_summary: A named plaza within Tapawingo Park beside the riverfront connection.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of West Lafayette identifies Myers Bridge Plaza as one of the facilities located within Tapawingo Park.
cards.source_title: City of West Lafayette — Tapawingo Park
cards.access_notes: Located within Tapawingo Park at 100 Tapawingo Dr.; follow park rules and observe the city’s 8 a.m. to post-sunset park hours.

cards.title: Riverside Skating Center
cards.subtitle: Tapawingo Drive riverfront corridor
cards.notes: Look for seasonal skating information at this named facility inside Tapawingo Park before building it into an outing.
cards.short_summary: A named skating facility situated within Tapawingo Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of West Lafayette lists the Riverside Skating Center among Tapawingo Park’s amenities and identifies the center as located in the park.
cards.source_title: City of West Lafayette — Tapawingo Park
cards.access_notes: Located within Tapawingo Park at 100 Tapawingo Dr. Check seasonal operations, skate availability, and any fees with the city before visiting.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Purdue traditions, from fountain runs and campus superstitions to songs, cheers and the annual kart race.

cards.title: Run the fountains
cards.subtitle: Engineering Fountain, Loeb Fountain and Stone Lions Fountains
cards.notes: During Boiler Gold Rush, follow the orientation route through the named fountains; treat this as a warm-weather campus walk and follow event guidance.
cards.short_summary: A Boiler Gold Rush rite of passage centered on Purdue’s fountains.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue University Residences calls running through the fountains a rite of passage and a key part of Boiler Gold Rush.
cards.access_notes: The source describes this as part of Boiler Gold Rush orientation; participate only through the organized program.

cards.title: Avoid walking beneath the Bell Tower
cards.subtitle: Purdue Bell Tower
cards.notes: Notice how this campus superstition shapes routes around the tower; it is folklore, not a graduation rule or academic requirement.
cards.short_summary: A modern Purdue superstition links the Bell Tower passageway with four-year graduation.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue University Residences documents the rumor that walking under the Bell Tower means not graduating within four years.
cards.access_notes: The university identifies this as a rumor/superstition, not an official policy.

cards.title: Seek the lionheads’ exam luck
cards.subtitle: Stone Lions Fountains, outside Stanley Coulter Hall
cards.notes: Find the four lion heads outside Stanley Coulter Hall and read the finals-week folklore; rely on preparation rather than any promised result.
cards.short_summary: A four-lion drinking-fountain superstition tied to final exams.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue University Residences says students believe drinking from all four lion heads will grant all A’s on final exams.
cards.access_notes: The university presents this as a superstition; the Stone Lions Fountains are outside Stanley Coulter Hall.

cards.title: Mark the first snow at Slayter Hill
cards.subtitle: Slayter Hill
cards.notes: When snow arrives, view the hill’s long-running sledding tradition from a safe distance or use appropriate sledding equipment and conditions.
cards.short_summary: First snowfall turns Slayter Hill into a memorable Purdue gathering point.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue University Residences states that Slayter Hill fills with students sledding on the day of the first snow.
cards.access_notes: Winter conditions vary; do not use improvised equipment or obstruct others.

cards.title: Catch Thrill on the Hill
cards.subtitle: Slayter Hill before football games
cards.notes: Check the football-weekend schedule, then hear the All-American Marching Band’s pre-game concert from Slayter Hill.
cards.short_summary: The marching band’s pre-game Slayter Hill concert anchors football Saturdays.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue University Residences identifies Thrill on the Hill as the Purdue All-American Marching Band’s pre-game concert at Slayter Hill.
cards.access_notes: Occurs during football season; consult current Purdue event information for timing.

cards.title: Remember the towering Homecoming displays
cards.subtitle: Historic residence-hall front-yard displays
cards.notes: Use this as a piece of Purdue history: explore archival images and Homecoming context rather than looking for an active display competition.
cards.short_summary: A former residence-hall display competition that shaped Purdue Homecoming memories.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue University Residences says the Homecoming display competition was launched in 1976 and discontinued in 1992.
cards.access_notes: Discontinued tradition: the display competition ended in 1992; Purdue still holds Homecoming events.

cards.title: Follow the Grand Prix
cards.subtitle: Purdue Grand Prix kart race
cards.notes: Watch for annual race information and learn how student teams prepare for the 160-lap competition and its associated campus activities.
cards.short_summary: Purdue’s student-centered annual kart-racing tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue Stories describes Grand Prix as a Purdue tradition in which 33 drivers and teams compete in a 160-lap race.
cards.access_notes: Annual event; consult current Grand Prix Foundation information for participation and spectator details.

cards.title: Ride the Boilermaker Special
cards.subtitle: Purdue’s official locomotive-style mascot
cards.notes: Look for official campus opportunities to ride the Boilermaker Special; the experience is documented as a student rite of passage.
cards.short_summary: A ride aboard Purdue’s official mascot has become a student milestone.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue Stories calls riding the Boilermaker Special, Purdue’s official mascot, a rite of passage for students.
cards.source_title: Purdue’s can’t-miss traditions for new Boilermakers
cards.access_notes: Rides depend on official availability and event operations; do not assume public access at a given time.

cards.title: Join in “Hail Purdue”
cards.subtitle: Purdue’s official fight song
cards.notes: Learn the chorus before a game or gathering, then join the song when it is led by Purdue’s bands or musical organizations.
cards.short_summary: Purdue’s fight song has been sung and clapped along with for more than a century.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue Stories states that “Hail Purdue” was adopted as Purdue’s official fight song and is sung at University functions.
cards.source_title: Boilermakers have played and sung ‘Hail Purdue’ across the globe — and even in space
cards.access_notes: A campus song tradition; performance timing depends on the event.

cards.title: Answer with “Boiler Up!”
cards.subtitle: Purdue’s rallying cry
cards.notes: Recognize the call in its game-day and campus context; Purdue’s style guide notes that fans use it as a greeting and in the fight song.
cards.short_summary: A 1997 football-era phrase that became Purdue’s ubiquitous rallying cry.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue states that Arnette Tiller introduced “Boiler Up” in 1997, fans greet one another with it, and it was incorporated into “Hail Purdue.”
cards.source_title: Purdue Brand Studio Editorial Style Guide
cards.access_notes: Use is informal and appropriate across Purdue events and digital campus communication.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Purdue University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A daylight-first, self-guided introduction to ten documented Purdue landmarks, art stops, and campus gathering places.

cards.title: Start at Purdue Memorial Union
cards.subtitle: Friday arrival · campus hub
cards.notes: Use the Union as your first indoor waypoint: look over the historic building, locate its services, and orient yourself at Grant Street and Mitch Daniels Boulevard.
cards.short_summary: Begin with Purdue’s central Union building.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue identifies the Purdue Memorial Union as a campus hub at the corner of Mitch Daniels Boulevard and Grant Street, with community spaces, events, and dining.
cards.access_notes: Check the Union’s current visitor and building information before entering or planning services.

cards.title: Spot the Degas bronzes
cards.subtitle: Friday arrival · Purdue Memorial Union
cards.notes: While in the Union, take a quiet art pause with the Degas bronzes. Treat it as a look-and-learn stop, then continue your campus walk.
cards.short_summary: See Purdue’s documented Degas bronze collection.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue states that the Degas Collection at Purdue consists of 74 posthumously cast bronze sculptures displayed in the Purdue Memorial Union.
cards.access_notes: The collection is displayed in the Purdue Memorial Union; verify building access for your visit.

cards.title: Walk through the Union Gateway
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Grant Street entrance
cards.notes: Step outside the Union and frame a photo from the gateway. Keep moving south or north from here to connect with the central campus walkways.
cards.short_summary: A named campus gateway beside the Union.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue lists the Purdue Memorial Union Gateway at the corner of Grant Street and Mitch Daniels Boulevard by the Purdue Memorial Union.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; use normal pedestrian routes and observe campus conditions.

cards.title: Pause in Academy Park
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · north of PMU and Stewart Center
cards.notes: Use the park as a short reset between landmarks. From its paths, identify Stewart Center and choose your next campus-facing direction before dusk.
cards.short_summary: Take a brief outdoor reset in the campus core.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue locates Academy Park north of the Purdue Memorial Union and Stewart Center.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor green space; visit during comfortable daylight conditions.

cards.title: Find the Unfinished Block P
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Academy Park
cards.notes: Approach the sculpture from Academy Park and read it as a reflective landmark. Photograph it respectfully, then continue toward nearby Stewart Center or the Mall.
cards.short_summary: Visit a documented bronze Purdue landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue identifies Unfinished Block P as a sculpture in Academy Park and describes it as a tribute to students unable to complete their degrees.
cards.source_title: Persistence personified: Campus art brings Boilermaker spirit to life
cards.access_notes: Outdoor memorial and sculpture; allow space for reflection and other visitors.

cards.title: Cross Purdue Mall
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · in front of Hovde Hall
cards.notes: Make this your broad-campus orientation walk. Follow the Mall at an easy pace, note building names, and use it to connect the academic core to later stops.
cards.short_summary: Traverse Purdue’s named central mall.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue locates Purdue Mall in front of Hovde Hall.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor pedestrian space; follow posted campus guidance and weather conditions.

cards.title: Meet Purdue’s Neil Armstrong statue
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · Neil Armstrong Hall of Engineering
cards.notes: Walk to the statue outside Armstrong Hall and look for the sculpted moon-boot impressions along the path before heading back through the engineering area.
cards.short_summary: An astronaut-themed engineering landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue says the Neil Armstrong statue stands outside Neil Armstrong Hall of Engineering and is positioned near a pathway of sculpted moon-boot impressions.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; access via campus pedestrian routes.

cards.title: Look for Brickhead Conversations
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · by Pao Hall
cards.notes: Add a compact public-art detour beside Pao Hall. Walk around both figures to take in the scale, then use Sheetz or Marsteller streets to continue.
cards.short_summary: A named two-figure public sculpture.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue identifies Brickhead Conversations as two figures located by Pao Hall between Sheetz and Marsteller streets.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public art; view from public walkways.

cards.title: See Ross-Ade Stadium
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · athletic district
cards.notes: Finish the daytime loop at the stadium exterior. Use the stop to recognize the athletic district, then check official event details separately before making game-day plans.
cards.short_summary: View Purdue’s football stadium from outside.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue identifies Ross-Ade Stadium as the home of the Purdue Boilermakers football team and a campus landmark.
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is appropriate; tickets and entry rules vary by event.

cards.title: End at Mackey Arena
cards.subtitle: Saturday late afternoon · athletic district
cards.notes: Close the first-weekend circuit at Mackey’s exterior near Ross-Ade. If an event interests you, consult official athletics information for current access and ticket details.
cards.short_summary: End the walk at Purdue’s basketball arena.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue identifies Mackey Arena as home to Purdue basketball and other major events, and notes its 1967 opening.
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is appropriate; event access and tickets vary.
